references.text: The connection with the preceding verses explains the purpose of the altar as a witness between the tribes
The altar is named as a witness that the Lord is God, confirming the testimony mentioned in this verse
A stone is set up as a witness between the people and God, similar to the use of a physical object as testimony
The heap of stones as a witness between Jacob and Laban, the same concept of a physical monument as a witness between parties
The law book placed as a witness against Israel, similar use of something physical as testimony for future generations
The instruction to make things according to the pattern (tavnit) shown on the mountain, the same Hebrew word for 'pattern/form'
The prohibition against offering sacrifices in any place, which is the background for the misunderstanding about the altar east of the Jordan
